definitions.gloss: training; practice; cultivating skill through repetition
definitions.explanation: Disciplined practice aimed at mastering a skill, especially in martial arts, qigong, and traditional Chinese-influenced physical or spiritual disciplines. Emphasizes the cultivation of inner skill through sustained effort.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{気功|きこう}の{練功|れんこう}をしている。
examples.english: I practice qigong training every morning.

examples.japanese: {太極拳|たいきょくけん}の{練功|れんこう}には{長年|ながねん}の{継続|けいぞく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Tai chi training requires years of continued practice.

examples.japanese: {師匠|ししょう}のもとで{練功|れんこう}を{重|かさ}ねて、ようやく{技|わざ}が{身|み}についた。
examples.english: After accumulating practice under my master, I finally internalized the techniques.

notes:
Composed of {練|れん} (to refine, to polish) and {功|こう} (skill, merit, achievement). Borrowed from Chinese {練功|れんこう} (liàngōng). While {練習|れんしゅう} is the general word for practice, {練功|れんこう} carries a more disciplined, meditative connotation associated with martial arts and body-mind cultivation traditions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {練功|れんこう}を{重|かさ}ねる: to accumulate practice
- {練功|れんこう}を{続|つづ}ける: to continue training
- {気功|きこう}の{練功|れんこう}: qigong practice
- {練功|れんこう}{場|じょう}: training ground

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {練習|れんしゅう}: practice — the general, everyday word for practicing any skill
- {修行|しゅぎょう}: ascetic training, discipline — training with a spiritual or character-building dimension
- {鍛錬|たんれん}: tempering, forging — rigorous physical or mental training to build strength
